conviction_note: Implied move 3.7% (straddle 3.83%, 37% spread) and a 7-of-7 up reaction history set abs_move 3.8; p_up 56 leans on a strong Q3 national industrial demand print (Cushman, 2026-10-09) and an upside-paid skew, held near 50 because the street's Q3 $1.58 already sits at the top of what the July guide implies, so a third raise is the bar rather than a surprise. The findings sum (+0.5) and the scaled number (+0.46) agree in sign and size.
bar: Company guide: FY2026 core FFO $6.22-6.30 (raised 2026-07-16, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001045609/000119312526305416/pld-ex99_2.htm). H1 actual $3.13 ($1.50 Q1 per https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045609/000119312526157977/pld-ex99_2.htm + $1.63 Q2), so the guide implies H2 $3.09-3.17, i.e. $1.545-1.585 a quarter. Q3 street consensus $1.58 non-GAAP on $2.21B revenue (Benzinga, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/PLD/earnings-forecasts, single source, snippet_only; a second source, tickerleague, shows $0.83 on 2 analysts, apparently GAAP EPS). The bar is anchored on the company guide; the quarterly consensus has one usable source, so findings that rest on it are capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest 18,474,881 shares at 2026-09-30 settlement, ~1.98% of 932.34m shares outstanding, 4.91 days to cover; up from 13,453,134 at 2026-07-15 (+37%), consistent with merger-arbitrage hedging of the SEGRO share offer (long SGRO / short PLD) rather than a fundamental short (Equibles/FINRA, https://equibles.com/stocks/pld/short-interest, read 2026-10-14). Not crowded. Skew_25d -5.34 vol points: calls bid over puts, 'upside paid'; put/call OI 0.52. Stock -11.3% from its 52-week high (153.35 on 2026-07-17, the day after the Q2 print), -0.47% over 20 days, +4.56% over 5 days into the print.

findings.finding: The street's Q3 core FFO bar ($1.58, Benzinga) sits at the top of what the company's own July guide implies: H1 core FFO was $3.13 ($1.50 + $1.63) against a FY guide of $6.22-6.30, leaving $1.545-1.585 a quarter for H2, and the guide sets net promote income at $0 for the year after +$0.03 in Q2 and -$0.02 in Q1, so H2 carries about -$0.01 of net promote. A merely in-line quarter at the guide midpoint ($1.565) would be a ~1% miss on the street number, so the street is already modelling a third raise.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance was raised at Q1 2026 (stock +1.72%) and Q2 2026 (+4.63%); Q2 beat $1.63 vs ~$1.53 consensus, partly promote-driven. The stock rose on all 7 prints in the baseline (median +1.84%, max +7.12%).
findings.why_not_priced: The arithmetic is public but aggregators quote the FY range, not the implied H2 quarterly run-rate; the sell-side Q3 number at $1.58 shows the street is already pricing upside to guidance. If the market were priced for an in-line quarter, the consensus would sit near $1.56 and the skew would not be call-bid. The risk is that a raise of only a few cents reads as 'met', not 'beat'.
findings.independence: Q1 figures from a separate 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045609/000119312526157977/pld-ex99_2.htm); consensus from Benzinga (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/PLD/earnings-forecasts). The guide and Q2 numbers share one document.

findings.finding: Cushman & Wakefield's Q3 2026 national industrial report (released 2026-10-09) put net absorption at 76.6m sq ft, the strongest quarter since Q1 2023, with year-to-date absorption above 203m sq ft and vacancy falling for a second consecutive quarter as demand outpaced supply. On the Q2 call (2026-07-16) Prologis assumed 220m sq ft of US absorption for the full year against 195m sq ft of completions, so nine months of Cushman data already sit at ~92% of PLD's full-year demand assumption, which supports occupancy, leasing and market-rent commentary and room to raise the occupancy/same-store guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 record leasing (67m sq ft) and occupancy up 20bp came with a guide raise and +4.63%; the stock has not been sold on improving operating metrics in the baseline (7 of 7 up).
findings.why_not_priced: It is a broker series, published, and partly priced. The stock fell ~13% from its July high on the SEGRO deal and rising rates, not on fundamentals, and the 20-day run-up is flat; if the market had fully priced an accelerating demand year, the stock would have recovered toward its July high rather than bouncing only 4.6% in five days. Different broker methods (Cushman vs PLD's own) make the comparison inexact, and Cushman's Q2 figure (62.1m sq ft in its July release) is inconsistent with the 'second straight quarter above 70m' line, suggesting a revision.
findings.independence: Proxy, not a company number. PLD's own assumption comes from the Q2 call transcript (https://www.webull.com/news/15238046746764288). Metro reports point mostly the same way: CBRE Dallas-Fort Worth Q3 2026 vacancy down to 7.8% (https://www.cbre.com/insights/figures/dallas-fort-worth-industrial-figures-q3-2026), with soft spots in Minneapolis and Tampa.

findings.finding: After the July 16 guide, Prologis sold 15.0m common shares (priced 2026-08-04, $138.75 net to the company) plus a 2.25m-share greenshoe, ~17.25m shares (~1.85% of shares outstanding) for ~$2.39bn net, earmarked for the SEGRO cash alternative, which does not close until H1 2027. Weighted over Aug-Dec that is ~0.7% more shares in 2026 (~$0.045 of FY core FFO) offset by ~$0.04 of interest on the parked proceeds at ~4%, so the per-share carry is near neutral, but none of it was in the July guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior PLD print has followed a large pre-funding equity raise in the baseline; the stock fell ~3% premarket on the deal-plus-raise announcement on 2026-08-04.
findings.why_not_priced: The raise itself is priced (the stock fell on it); what is not visible is whether management absorbs the share count and still raises the per-share guide. If the share count were a worry, the Q3 consensus would sit below the guide midpoint, and it sits above it. What the money buys: the cash leg of a deal management calls 'broadly neutral to minimally dilutive' to core FFO in year one, so it is a small negative or zero, not distress.
findings.independence: Same transaction in the 424B2 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001045609/000110465926090715/tm2621155-6_424b2.htm) and the 2026-08-04 8-K term-loan filing (https://www.boardroomalpha.com/sec/pld-8-k-2026-08-04-0001104659-26-089980); one fact, one finding.

findings.finding: SEGRO shareholders approved the scheme at the court and general meetings on 2026-09-28, so the £14bn all-share combination (0.0920 PLD shares per SEGRO share, capped £3.5bn cash alternative, completion H1 2027, long stop 2027-08-04) is past its main vote. The Q3 call is the first earnings forum where management can discuss the deal: it declined to on the Q2 call, and it has called the deal 'broadly neutral to minimally dilutive' to core FFO in the first full year after synergies.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock is down ~10% since the last print and ~13% from its 2026-07-17 high, a drawdown that began with the 2026-08-04 deal and equity announcement; no prior print has carried a pending large M&A discussion.
findings.why_not_priced: The vote is public; the open question is whether management uses the call to quantify synergies and the 2027 earnings bridge, which the market has discounted as dilutive since August. If the overhang were cleared, the stock would trade back toward its pre-deal ~$144 (the 2026-08-03 close in the prospectus) rather than $133. The sign is uncertain: more detail could also confirm dilution, hence the wide range.
findings.independence: Deal terms and accretion language: Prologis release (https://ir.prologis.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1049/prologis-announces-recommended-acquisition-of-segro-plc); the Q2 call's refusal to discuss it is in the transcript (https://www.webull.com/news/15238046746764288).

findings.finding: Short interest rose from 13.45m shares (2026-07-15) to 18.47m (2026-09-30), ~2% of shares and 4.9 days to cover, a build timed with the SEGRO share offer and consistent with merger-arbitrage hedges that do not trade on earnings; with skew_25d at -5.34 (calls bid) and put/call OI 0.52, the options market leans up into a name that has risen on 7 of 7 prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is by definition partly priced; the read is that the SI build is a hedge rather than a fundamental bet, so it is not a negative a print can confirm. If it were a fundamental short, days to cover would be rising into the print, and it fell from 6.04 to 4.91.
findings.independence: Skew and OI from the sealed baseline (Yahoo options, 2026-10-14); SI from FINRA via Equibles. The arbitrage reading is an inference from the deal timing (https://www.boardroomalpha.com/sec/pld-8-k-2026-08-04-0001104659-26-089980).

findings.finding: On the Q2 call management said the embedded lease mark-to-market held at 17% and 'will come down' toward low double digits over time; Q2 net effective rent change was 36.9% (cash 22.3%), so Q3 rent-change spreads are more likely to compress than expand.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Rent-change spreads have drifted down from 2023 peaks while the stock still rose on every print in the baseline, so this line has not driven reactions.
findings.why_not_priced: Management already guided the market to it, so it is mostly priced; it sits inside what the company told investors to expect. Filed for completeness: if the market were surprised by it, analysts would not have raised targets after Q2 (e.g. RBC upgrade to Outperform, $160, early August).
findings.independence: Q2 rent-change figures from the 8-K exhibit (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001045609/000119312526305416/pld-ex99_2.htm); same call/document family as finding 1 for the guide, but a different line.

outside_window.finding: SEGRO combination still needs High Court sanction and antitrust/regulatory approvals; completion expected H1 2027, long stop 2027-08-04 (extendable to 2028-04-04). SEGRO's own Q3 trading update (last year's was 2025-10-21) may land after the window.

baseline_tension: What I found mostly agrees with the call-bid skew and the 7-of-7 up history (strong Q3 national demand, deal vote passed), but the street's quarterly bar already sits at the top of the guide-implied run-rate and the stock's drawdown is driven by SEGRO dilution and rates, which a print does not resolve, so p_up is held at 56 rather than higher.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (bar has one quarterly estimate source): the consensus-at-top-of-guide finding was capped from -0.5 to -0.4
Rule 5 (proxy, not a company number): the Cushman national absorption finding was cut from +0.8 to +0.6, filed with independence marked as proxy
Rule 4 (financing is a question): the equity raise buys the SEGRO cash leg with near-neutral per-share carry, so it was cut from -0.2 to -0.1
Rule 6 (inside what the company guided): the rent-spread compression that management flagged moved from -0.2 to -0.1
Rules 1 and 7 left p_up (56) and abs_move (3.8) unchanged: the history rewards prints and the skew agrees with the sign
